challenges.name: traits-derive-display-quiz
challenges.title: Derives, Display and trait bounds
challenges.description: Predict what derived traits do, and decide which programs the compiler accepts once traits, Display and generic bounds are involved.

questions.explanation: A derived Ord on an enum orders the variants in the order they are declared: Standard < Express < SameDay. sort() therefore gives [Standard, Express, Express, SameDay], and dedup() removes consecutive equal elements (it uses PartialEq), leaving [Standard, Express, SameDay]. SameDay > Express is true because SameDay is declared later. The derive never sorts by the variant names, so [Express, SameDay, Standard] (alphabetical) is wrong. dedup only removes neighbours that are equal, and after sorting the two Express values are neighbours, so the duplicate does not survive. The program compiles: Ord and PartialOrd are exactly what sort() and > need.

options.text: It does not compile: enums cannot be compared with >

questions.question: Each option is a complete program compiled with rustc --edition 2024. Which of them compile? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Implementing fmt::Display compiles, and it also gives the type a to_string() method for free. A struct with derive(PartialEq, Eq, Hash) can be a HashMap key, because a HashMap needs exactly Eq and Hash on its keys. A trait with a default method compiles even when the impl writes only the required method: Document gets price_text() from the trait. derive(Debug) alone does not make {} work: the compiler reports error[E0277]: `Parcel` doesn't implement `std::fmt::Display`. derive(Clone, Copy) on a struct with a String field is error[E0204]: the trait `Copy` cannot be implemented for this type, because a String owns heap memory and cannot be copied bit by bit. A generic function cannot use > on a T without a bound: error[E0369]: binary operation `>` cannot be applied to type `T`, and the compiler suggests T: PartialOrd.

challenges.name: route-sheet-labels-and-prices
challenges.title: Labels and prices for the route sheet
challenges.description: The evening route sheet prints documents and packages in their Debug form, and every price is 0. Implement the Priced trait for Document (15000 VND, 25000 VND for express) and Package (20000 VND up to 1000 g, plus 5000 VND for every started 500 g above that), implement fmt::Display for both ("DN-07-0413 document (express)", "DN-07-0412 package 1.25 kg"), and write the generic fn total<T: Priced>(items: &[T]) -> u64. The test runner reads one item per line and prints every label with its price, then the totals per kind.
